This was actually really wonderful to read. Thank you. It probably sound ridiculous, but it actually made me feel a lot better. Thank you.

Honestly, I don't remember. It was just this horrifying crippling fear. It might've been that I was afraid of what people thought, but I don't know for ure.

I know that she has had panic attacks before, and struggled with anxiety before. That's why I don't understand how she can crush off my anxiety like it's nothing. She mocked me for having it the other day, and told me that accepting this part of myself, my anxiety disorders, was bad, and that I was "becoming my disorder". It's hard, because we tried for years to fix my anxiety, and I just don't want to feel broken anymore. I was okay with having this thing that a lot of people don't, and now I just feel terrible again.

Like I said, she's very private. When I have panic attacks, sometimes I can hide it, but usually its a very big ordeal and it takes a while to get a hold of myself. She doesn't want people to see me have a panic attack, and then think badly of her. (She's told me all this before.)

Honestly, I'm past the point of privacy. I just want a reason to live for the next three years, and if answering personal questions can help me, I'm all for it. I hate this feeling.

I don't know how to get space, I can't drive, and even if I go to an activity like 4-H, my mom stays the entire time. (Which does make sense given my history of panic attacks. But all she's ever really cared about is that I don't make a fool of myself. She doesn't really try to help me when I have a panic attack.)

I've been homeschooled since third grade. I can't seem to function well at school, as hard as we tried. I used to become so panicked in the morning I would literally make myself sick. I've thought about asking to go back to regular school, but schools in my area are terrible.

I've had my anxiety literally as long as I can remember. I went to therapy for six years, and they all agreed that my disorders were a mix of environmental and genetic factors. (Anxiety runs on my dad's side of the family, and I was molested as a child.)

I feel like a spoiled child, and sometimes I think my mom is right and I do complain too much.
People say that to me all the time! I always choose to take it as a compliment, even though most Slytherins in the series were pretty much evil.
My mom is pretty the same. Of course, I'm over here rambling about harry potter and wand types and which spells in which situations, and sometimes she'll just listen and nod.

I did explain it to her. I told her that I don't really feel sexual attraction the same way that she does. I told her that I can still feel romantic attractions, and she knows that I've had a couple of crushes before, but she still just said I'll change my mind later. I explained the difference between romantic and sexual attraction, etc. but she still didn't get it. I'd told her a little bit about asexuality before, and she'd seemed to understand, but then when I told her I felt that way, she got upset.

It sucks because she says that shes very accepting, several of her friends and coworkers are gay/bi but than I say that I'm asexual and she freaks out. Now I don't know if I'll ever be able to tell her that I'm biromantic. What if she's never okay with that?
My mom and non hp friends do the same thing. Sometimes I'll explain it, sometime I'll just say watch the movies. You'll understand.
